title: English teacher salary in Vietnam (2026): rates and take-home
description: Hourly and monthly pay by employer type in Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Da Nang, mostly from 2026 job ads, with take-home pay worked out under the new tax rules.
h1: What English teachers earn in Vietnam in 2026, and what you keep after tax
intro: Most foreign English teachers in Vietnam are paid by the hour. In 2026 Ho Chi Minh City job ads, language centres and public-school agencies pay similar hourly rates, and a full-time load of 78–95 teaching hours a month turns them into a salary. Bilingual schools advertise US$1,700–3,000 a month; premium international schools pay licensed teachers about US$2,500–4,000+. Under 2026 rules a tax resident on a 12-month contract keeps about 86% of a mid-range full-time centre salary after tax and social insurance.
keyPoints: In July–October 2026 job ads, Ho Chi Minh City language centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour; most new-teacher offers sit at {{vnd:430000-560000}}. 'Up to' figures are ceilings, and most ads do not say gross or net.
A full-time centre load of about 78–95 contact hours a month comes to roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross. VUS counts 12–18 hours a week as part-time.

Under the 2026 rules a resident earning {{vnd:45000000}} gross on a 12-month contract takes home about {{vnd:38700000}}: 9.5% social insurance, then 5–35% income tax after a {{vnd:15500000}} monthly personal deduction. Non-residents pay a flat 20%.
Hanoi pays the same as Saigon or slightly more in 2026 ads; Da Nang pays similar hourly rates but has fewer jobs, and some chains want 3+ years' experience there.

Hourly pay usually stops when classes stop: the June–August public-school summer, the Tet closure and cancelled classes. Get a minimum-hours guarantee in writing and keep two to three months' costs in reserve.
A 13th-month salary or Tet bonus is not required by law. Completion bonuses are the most common bonus in ads (one month's pay, or {{vnd:11500000-13500000}}) and are usually lost if you leave early.

sections.title: How much English teachers earn, by type of job (2026)

blocks.text: Most figures below come from July–October 2026 employer job ads and recruitment pages. The exceptions are marked: the international-school band comes from pay guides such as Spill.org's, the corporate client rate from an agency's price list, the university rate from an RMIT ad that closed in December 2023, and one corporate figure from about 2024. Vietnam publishes **no official statistics on foreign teachers' pay**, so ads are the best evidence there is. Most do not say whether pay is gross or net, 'up to' figures are ceilings, and some employers quote US dollars, so treat each range as the start of a question rather than a promise.

blocks.text: Sources: [Vietnam Teaching Jobs' Ho Chi Minh City listings](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh), [VUS's teacher FAQ](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979), [a 2026–27 public-school agency ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/foreign-esl-teachers-for-public-schools-in-ho-chi-minh-city-2026-2027/), [an EIV kindergarten ad](https://teast.co/job/full-time-homeroom-kindergarten-teacher-go-vap-district-Ow6XNeTaalIIPg66rO3U), [Pathway School's ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/expat-primary-teacher-pathway-school-district-2-hcmc-full-time), [Spill.org's international-school pay bands](https://spill.org/en/guides/ho-chi-minh-city-vietnam-expat-guide), [RMIT's hourly educator ad](https://vn.linkedin.com/jobs/view/english-language-educators-hourly-hcmc-hanoi-and-danang-at-rmit-university-3673867344), [BYAN's 2026 price list](https://byan.com.vn/vn/bang-gia-cung-cap-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai) and [Cambly's tutor FAQ](https://support.cambly.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055993652-Prospective-Tutors-FAQs).

For the detail behind the two biggest rows, see [working at a language centre in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/language-centre-jobs-in-ho-chi-minh-city) and [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam). IELTS-focused centres are left out of the table because we found no solid 2026 pay data for them.

Check where an 'HCMC' job actually is. Since 1 July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City has included the former Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces ([SGGP on Resolution 202/2025/QH15](https://www.sggp.org.vn/thanh-lap-tphcm-moi-post801737.html)), and official addresses now use new ward names, while ads still say 'District 1' or 'Binh Thanh'. A job tagged HCMC can be 30–200+ km from District 1. Some of these jobs pay a location allowance — DTP adds {{vnd:2000000}} a month in Thu Dau Mot and Tan Uyen — and some job boards file provincial campuses under 'Hồ Chí Minh', so confirm the campus address before you compare pay.

sections.title: What an hourly rate adds up to in a month

blocks.text: VUS defines full-time as 20–25 teaching hours a week and part-time as 12–18 ([VUS teacher FAQ](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)). Apollo's full-time load was about 78–95 contact hours a month in [a 2024 Apollo listing](https://www.seriousteachers.com/job_details/278256/0/vietnamesl-teacher-teachers-needed-now-in-vietnam-vietnam). The rate normally covers **contact time only**: planning, meetings, early arrival and travel between schools are typically unpaid, and in schools an 'hour' may be a 35–45-minute period.

blocks.caption: Monthly gross for hourly teachers: hours taught × rate, our arithmetic on 2026 advertised rates, before tax and insurance
rows: Part-time centre teacher, about 14 hours a week
Public-school agency, about 15 hours a week

blocks.text: Some employers now advertise guaranteed pay rather than purely hourly pay: Wall Street English offers part-timers a 'guaranteed monthly salary' ([its May 2026 ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/ho-chi-minh-city-part-time-native-english-teachers-2)), and Apollo Hanoi and DTP advertise guaranteed salary or hours. None publishes the guaranteed amount, so ask for it in writing.

blocks.title: Hourly pay stops when classes stop
blocks.text: Many hourly arrangements pay only for hours actually taught, with nothing for cancelled classes, the Tet closure or the June–August public-school summer. Public schools teach about 35 weeks a year, opening on 5 September and finishing before 31 May ([MOET's 2026 framework](https://baolaocai.vn/bo-giao-duc-va-dao-tao-cong-bo-khung-ke-hoach-thoi-gian-nam-hoc-post905643.html)). Part-timers on a labour contract have the same rights as full-timers under the Labour Code, but on a service agreement they may not, so check which you are signing. Get a minimum-hours or minimum-pay guarantee in writing and keep two to three months' living costs in reserve.

sections.title: From gross to take-home: income tax and social insurance

blocks.text: Two deductions come off a teacher's gross pay. **Social insurance** is compulsory for foreign employees on labour contracts of 12 months or more: you pay 9.5% (8% pension plus 1.5% health insurance) and the employer pays 20.5% ([EY tax alert](https://www.ey.com/en_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/people-advisory-service-tax-alert-june-2025-notable-points-regarding-the-mandatory-social-security-from-1-july-2025)). Contributions are capped at {{vnd:50600000}} a month of salary from 1 July 2026 ([Ha Tinh provincial portal on the new base salary](https://hatinh.gov.vn/vi/bai-viet/tang-luong-co-so-tu-0172026)).

**Income tax** follows PIT Law 109/2025/QH15. For residents, 2026 monthly taxable income is taxed at 5% up to {{vnd:10000000}}, 10% to {{vnd:30000000}}, 20% to {{vnd:60000000}}, 30% to {{vnd:100000000}} and 35% above, after a personal deduction of {{vnd:15500000}} a month and {{vnd:6200000}} per registered dependant ([KPMG on the new PIT law](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/vn/pdf/2026/01/new-pit-law-en.pdf)). Non-residents pay a flat 20% with no deductions. You are resident if you spend 183 days or more in Vietnam in a calendar year or in the 12 consecutive months from your arrival ([Decree 253/2026/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/180507251028987904/2026/7/16/469959-1784171413_v1_1784174315_signed.pdf)).

blocks.caption: Monthly take-home under 2026 rules, resident with no dependants unless stated: our calculation from PIT Law 109/2025/QH15 and the 9.5% employee insurance rate
rows: 12-month contract, salary above the insurance cap
Contract under 12 months, no social insurance

blocks.text: Under the 2025 rules (seven brackets and an {{vnd:11000000}} personal deduction) the same {{vnd:45000000}} teacher kept about {{vnd:36400000}}, so the 2026 changes are worth a little over {{vnd:2000000}} a month at that level. On a labour contract under 12 months neither social nor health insurance is compulsory for a foreign employee (the amended Health Insurance Law 51/2024/QH15 applies the same 12-month test), so nothing is deducted for either and you need private health cover; if your payslip shows an insurance deduction anyway, ask HR what it is for.
What changes the numbers

items: **Your first months.** For foreigners the employer withholds at progressive rates if your contract covers 183 days or more in the tax year, and at 20% if it covers fewer ([Decree 253/2026/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/180507251028987904/2026/7/16/469959-1784171413_v1_1784174315_signed.pdf)). If you were taxed at 20% and then became resident, the year-end finalisation settles the difference.

**January–June 2026 pay.** Returns for those months were filed under the old seven-bracket scale and are not re-filed. Any refund from the new scale comes only through the 2026 finalisation, so if you leave Vietnam in 2026, finalise before you go.

**'Net' and 'tax-free' offers.** A net offer means the employer pays your tax and insurance, so compare offers net to net. 'Tax-free' in a recruiter's ad usually means the school pays the tax, not that the income is exempt.
**Service agreements.** Residents paid without a labour contract, or on one shorter than 3 months, usually have 10% withheld from each payment of {{vnd:5000000}} or more, settled at finalisation.

**Benefits.** Overtime within the legal limits, and pay for unused leave when you leave a job, are now fully tax-exempt. One home-leave flight a year and children's school fees paid by the employer are not taxable. Rent the employer pays to the landlord is taxed only up to 15% of your other taxable income, but a cash housing allowance is taxed in full.

blocks.text: Social insurance is not all lost. When your labour contract ends or your work permit expires without renewal, you can claim a lump sum of 2 months' average contribution salary for each year contributed ([Social Insurance Law 41/2024/QH15](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/law-41-2024-qh15-on-social-insurance-360809-d1.html)). The [personal income tax guide](/teach-in-vietnam/personal-income-tax-for-teachers-in-vietnam) covers residency, finalisation and dependants, and the [social and health insurance guide](/teach-in-vietnam/social-and-health-insurance-for-foreign-teachers-in-vietnam) covers the lump-sum claim. Your employer's payroll and the tax office have the final word on your own case.

sections.title: Ho Chi Minh City vs Hanoi vs Da Nang: who pays more?

blocks.text: In 2026 ads **Hanoi pays the same as Saigon or slightly more**, and Da Nang pays similar hourly rates with far fewer jobs. Claims that Saigon pays 10–15% more are not supported by current ads, and published guides disagree with each other on city averages, so treat those as marketing estimates ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs salary guide](https://blog.vietnamteachingjobs.com/average-salary-esl-teachers-vietnam/)).

In July–October 2026 ads, Hanoi employers offered {{vnd:550000-650000}} an hour and the two Da Nang ads {{vnd:500000-570000}}, against the Saigon centre range above. Tax and social insurance are national, so the same gross gives the same net in every city; the real differences are rent and the number of jobs, compared employer by employer in [Hanoi vs Ho Chi Minh City (and Da Nang)](/teach-in-vietnam/hanoi-vs-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers#what-each-city-pays).

sections.title: What moves your pay: experience, qualifications and passport

blocks.text: Experience

Centre ads advertise new-teacher rates and 'up to' ceilings, and few publish a pay scale; Wall Street English offers an annual performance-based raise and The English Connection in Hanoi mentions 'salary progression'. Experience matters more for **which employers will hire you** than for the hourly rate: RMIT required 3 years after CELTA, and ILA asks for 3+ years for Da Nang, Nha Trang and Vung Tau. At international schools experience shows in the salary band: Spill.org puts early-career teachers at US$2,000–2,800 a month and established teachers at US$2,800–4,000.
Qualifications

No 2025–2026 Ho Chi Minh City ad publishes a pay premium for CELTA, and most centres accept [any 120-hour TEFL](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam). What a CELTA buys is entry to the better-paying employers: RMIT required it, and Wall Street English 'strongly prefers' CELTA or Trinity. The only premium figure we found is old and second-hand: a 2019 British Council summer-school ad reportedly paid DELTA holders about 13% more than CELTA holders. A teaching licence (B.Ed, PGCE, QTS or a US licence) is what opens the US$2,000–4,000 monthly salaries at international schools and some bilingual schools (SSG Education asked for one).
Passport and native-speaker status

Vietnamese law sets conditions for foreign workers on age, qualifications, health, criminal record and a work permit, and none on nationality ([Labour Code 2019, Art. 151](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html)). Employers still set preferences: some VUS and Wall Street English ads list eligible passports, while VUS also considers non-native speakers who send an intro video and RMIT accepts non-native speakers with IELTS Academic 8.0. Where an ad publishes both rates the gap is visible: [DTP's September 2025 public-school ad](https://teast.co/job/expat-english-teachers-part-time-in-hcmc-sep-2025-Loyb1krhwvW4nfFHJFHR) offered non-native teachers up to {{vnd:525000}} an hour against up to {{vnd:550000}} for native speakers. Its 2026 ad lists a single range. [Hiring bias in teaching jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/discrimination-and-hiring-bias-in-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam) covers how this plays out and what to do about it.

blocks.text: The leave and bonus rules are in the [Labour Code 2019](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html). Most foreign-teacher contracts at centres do not include a Tet bonus. Whether an hourly teacher is actually paid for public holidays depends on the contract type, so ask.

sections.title: What you can save on a teacher's salary in Saigon

blocks.text: Savings depend more on rent and hours than on the hourly rate. On eno.vn's budgets a frugal single teacher in a private room spends about {{vnd:14000000-17000000}} a month and a comfortable one in a one-bedroom flat about {{vnd:25000000-35000000}}; against full-time take-home pay of about {{vnd:30500000-44300000}}, that leaves roughly {{vnd:13500000-30300000}} a month on the frugal budget and anything from nothing to about {{vnd:19300000}} on the comfortable one ([cost of living guide](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers#what-you-can-save)).

Those are full months, before flights home, a motorbike, health cover beyond the public scheme and the months when hourly income drops. Budget the first month separately: a rental deposit, furnishing and the wait for your first pay, which teachers report usually arrives in arrears around the 5th–10th of the following month.

sections.title: How to compare offers and make sure you get paid

items.title: Turn the rate into a month
items.text: Multiply the rate by the hours you are actually timetabled, not the hours promised. Ask for the next four weeks' timetable and a written minimum-hours or minimum-pay guarantee.

items.title: Ask the four questions most ads skip
items.text: Is it gross or net? Per 60-minute hour or per 35–45-minute period? Are planning, meetings and admin paid? Is it paid in US dollars or đồng, and at which exchange rate and on which date? Employers may pay foreign staff in foreign currency, but tax and insurance are worked out in đồng.

items.title: Check the contract type and the legal minimums
items.text: A labour contract brings social insurance (at 12 months or more), paid holidays and the Labour Code's protections; a service agreement usually does not. Probation lasts at most 60 days at no less than 85% of pay, and an employer may not keep your original documents or take a deposit. See [English teaching contracts: what to check](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

items.title: Fix the pay date and keep your own records
items.text: Under Labour Code Art. 97, hourly-paid workers are paid after each period or in an agreed lump sum at least every 15 days, and monthly-paid workers on a fixed agreed date. Keep a log of every class you teach, with dates and minutes.

items.title: Check the employer
items.text: The Apax Leaders chain left foreign teachers unpaid: at least 81 of them said they were owed {{vnd:13400000000}} in total ([Stockbiz](https://stockbiz.vn/tin-tuc/ibc-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-het-hy-vong-duoc-apax-leaders-tra-no-luong/24554112)), and a Dak Lak centre closed in 2026 owing teachers' wages. Ask current teachers whether pay has been on time, and check the employer's page in eno.vn's [school directory](/schools), where teachers who worked or interviewed there can leave reviews (most schools have few or no reviews yet). Jobs on [eno.vn's jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) open the original posting; eno.vn has not verified those employers, and you should never pay to get a job.

items.title: If pay is late or missing
items.text: If wages are 15 or more days late, the employer owes interest on top, and if you are not paid in full or on time you may end a labour contract without notice. Final pay is due within 14 working days of the contract ending. Wage complaints in the city go to the [HCMC Department of Home Affairs](https://www.sggp.org.vn/tphcm-thanh-lap-7-so-moi-post782716.html); a labour mediator usually comes first and must be asked within 6 months, and court claims lapse after 1 year.

faqs.q: Are public-school English teachers paid during the summer break?
faqs.a: Usually not if you are paid by the hour. Public schools teach about 35 weeks a year, from late August in Ho Chi Minh City (pupils report on 24 August, first and final grades on 17 August; the opening ceremony is 5 September) to before 31 May, and no 2025-2026 agency ad we found promised summer pay. Ask the agency about summer camps or a retainer, and save for June to August.

faqs.q: Do teachers in Vietnam get a 13th-month salary?
faqs.a: Not by law. Under Labour Code Article 104 each employer sets its own bonus rules, so a 13th month or Tet bonus is enforceable only if your contract or the employer's published bonus policy promises one. Foreign-teacher ads usually offer completion bonuses instead.

faqs.q: Can my school pay me in US dollars?
faqs.a: Yes. The Labour Code lets employers pay foreign employees in foreign currency, but tax and social insurance are calculated in đồng. Ask which exchange rate and which date will be used, because a bank's buying and selling rates for the dollar differ.

faqs.q: What happens to my pay if I quit before the contract ends?
faqs.a: You usually lose any completion or KPI bonus. On a 12-36-month contract you must give 30 days' notice, and quitting unlawfully costs half a month's salary plus pay for the notice days you skipped. If the school has not paid you in full or on time, you can leave without notice.

faqs.q: How much can I earn teaching online on top of my job?
faqs.a: Not much per hour: Cambly pays US$10.20 an hour (US$12 on Cambly Kids), with no guaranteed hours and gaps between calls unpaid. If you are a Vietnamese tax resident, you must declare income yourself when it comes from a foreign platform that is not tax-registered in Vietnam.

faqs.q: Do I get my social insurance back when I leave Vietnam?
faqs.a: You can claim a one-off lump sum when your labour contract ends or your work permit expires without renewal. It is 2 months of your average contribution salary for each year you contributed, and there is no 12-month waiting period for foreigners.
